we have proposed and analyzed a new class of hidden Markov errors in variables models, we have derived a maximum likelihood (ML)-based recursive algorithm to estimate the parameters in this class of models, we have shown the consistency of this recursive algorithm, we have derived an alternative recursive algorithm based on the gradient of the log-likelihood function, and we have shown the convergence of this second algorithm.
We propose two on-line algorithms, based on stochastic approximation, for estimating errors-in-variables Markovian models.
we propose two on-line algorithms for estimating hidden Markov errors in variables (HMEIV) models.
In summary, our research is concerned with
estimation of errors in variable models with Markovian disturbances using the EM algorithm, stochastic approximation, and gradient-based methods.
the development of iterative and recursive estimators of errors in variables (EIV) models with finite state Markovian disturbances, and the application of these estimators to speech recognition.

the following three aspects of hidden Markov models with errors-in-variables: (1) maximum likelihood estimation of the model parameters using the EM algorithm, (2) recursive or on-line estimation of such models, and (3) the application of these models to speech processing and communication systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recursive algorithms are useful in situations where the data are collected sequentially and the EM algorithm cannot be applied because it requires all the data at once.
both on-line algorithms are useful for on-line estimation of errors in-variables models.
the gradient-based algorithm is more accurate and faster than the EM-based algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have derived the ML estimates of errors-in-variables model with Markovian disturbances using the EM algorithm, then two recursive or on-line algorithms have been proposed.
we propose two recursive estimation schemes for estimating hidden Markov errors in variables models.

we have derived the EM algorithm for estimating the parameters of a general class of hidden Markov models with errors-in-variables, and then derived two on-line or recursive estimation schemes for such models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EM algorithm can be easily modified to derive recursive or on-line estimators.

the recursive or "on line" estimation schemes are computationally efficient and can be used to estimate the errors in variables model with finite-state Markowian disturbances in real-time applications.
